value.rationale: The sample Gini mean difference measures scale/dispersion via all sample pairs, while an individual sample quantile is a natural single-order-summary. Determining which quantile most strongly co-moves in Pearson correlation under exponential sampling is motivated and has a precise nonobvious answer: a sharp rank fraction near 93.006% with maximal limiting correlation about 0.822. The all-ranks convergence and endpoint exclusion supply an actual classification, not a selected numerical slice. No downstream theorem or predictive optimality outside Pearson linear association is asserted.
